subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-party agent teleconference lifecycle layer now, and what storage, transcript privacy, and authorization boundary should it use?
rationale: The issue is a concrete feature RFC, but it adds core CLI/API surface, durable cross-agent state, transcript artifacts, and a new config shape, which cannot be selected safely without maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Keep narrow design open
options.body: Keep this issue as the scoped product/security design anchor and require a future PR to use current storage policy plus explicit auth and transcript boundaries.

options.title: Move to plugin/API gap
options.body: Defer core verbs and first prove whether an external plugin can implement the meeting layer with existing SDK surfaces or a smaller SDK extension.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Reject first-party meeting lifecycle work for now and point contributors to standalone ClawHub/plugin experiments until maintainers sponsor it.

recommendation.title: Keep narrow design open
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the scoped product/security design anchor and require a future PR to use current storage policy plus explicit auth and transcript boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the maintainer shaping comment and also appears in current A2A helper history, so he is the best available routing owner for the product-direction question.
